newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican unveils restored 1930 Papal car.
newsitem.headline: Vatican unveils restored 1930 Papal car.

text.p: The Vatican on Thursday unveiled a lovingly restored 1930 limousine with one careful owner -- the late Pope Pius XI.

The plush bordeaux and black Citroen Lictoria is a collector's dream. It has clocked only 155 km (96 miles) in 66 years. The current Pontiff, John Paul II, has sometimes moved more than that in a few hours in one of his limousines.

Pope Pius XI received the car as a gift from its French makers only a year after he stopped being a "Prisoner of the Vatican" -- confined to the tiny city-state because of a territorial conflict with Italy that lasted from 1870 to 1929.
In 1930 when he received the car, Pope Pius was taken for a brief ride around the Vatican gardens and said it showed that modern things were sometimes useful.
He and his successors rarely used the car after that.
The car, with plate number SCV (Vatican City State) 5, will be housed in the Vatican museums alongside the ornate horse-drawn carriages that transported Pontiffs before the automobile age.
